skill.name: Quality Gates Skill
skill.description: Assess task complexity, validate requirements, and apply quality gates before implementation begins.
skill.summary: A structured framework for stopping unclear work, escalating blockers, and planning complex tasks.
skill.author: ArieGoldkin

content.value_statement: Unclear requirements and large tasks cause rework and stalled delivery. This skill provides repeatable checks for complexity, dependencies, evidence, and escalation before work continues.
actual_capabilities: Scores tasks on a five-level complexity scale using scope, dependencies, and uncertainty.
Checks requirements, dependencies, failed attempts, and evidence before implementation proceeds.
Provides templates for gate checks, requirements reviews, complexity assessments, and escalations.
Breaks level four and five work into smaller subtasks with dependencies and acceptance criteria.
Escalates blocked work after repeated failed attempts or unresolved critical questions.
limitations: It provides a decision framework and does not inspect repositories or run tests automatically.
Complexity scores and estimates depend on accurate task information.
It does not replace human approval for product, security, or architectural decisions.
Its example context code requires adaptation to the host agent environment.

use_cases.title: Plan a new feature
use_cases.description: Review requirements and dependencies before a developer begins a multi-file feature.

use_cases.title: Triage an agent task
use_cases.description: Decide whether an AI agent should proceed, ask questions, or escalate a blocked task.

use_cases.title: Prepare a delivery plan
use_cases.description: Split a large initiative into testable subtasks with clear dependencies and acceptance criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Run a quick gate check
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a quality gate for this task: [task]. Identify complexity, unanswered critical questions, dependencies, and a pass, warning, or blocked decision.

prompt_templates.title: Review feature requirements
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the requirements checklist for [feature]. List missing happy-path, error-handling, input-validation, API, and acceptance requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Break down complex work
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess [initiative] as a level 4 or 5 task. Break it into level 1 to 3 subtasks, map dependencies, and define acceptance criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Escalate a stalled task
prompt_templates.prompt: I tried [task] three times. Build a stuck-task escalation with the attempted approaches, current blocker, unanswered questions, and recommended next action.

output_examples.input: Run a quality gate for adding account export to the application.
output: Complexity: Level 4 because the work spans permissions, data selection, and export delivery.
Gate status: Blocked until retention rules, export format, and authorization requirements are confirmed.
Next action: Ask the product owner to define the missing requirements.

output_examples.input: Break down a new payment integration.
output: Subtask 1: Define provider contract and acceptance criteria.
Subtask 2: Implement payment flow after the contract is approved.
Subtask 3: Add failure handling and end-to-end verification.

best_practices: Run a gate check before starting work, especially for level three to five tasks.
Record assumptions when proceeding with warnings and validate them early.
Escalate after repeated failures instead of repeating the same approach.
anti_patterns: Starting a complex task without confirmed requirements or a task breakdown.
Treating a blocked gate as permission to continue without resolving blockers.
Ignoring warning conditions without documenting assumptions and risks.

faq.question: What is a quality gate?
faq.answer: A quality gate is a structured decision to pass, warn, or block work based on readiness evidence.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it before new work, when requirements are unclear, after repeated failures, or before complex implementation.

faq.question: How are tasks scored?
faq.answer: Tasks use a one-to-five scale based on scope, file changes, dependencies, estimates, and unknowns.

faq.question: What blocks a task?
faq.answer: More than three critical unknowns, missing dependencies, failed evidence, repeated failures, or an unplanned complex task can block work.

faq.question: Can I proceed with a warning?
faq.answer: Yes. Document assumptions, verify the approach early, and schedule a checkpoint for review.

faq.question: Does this skill run tests or change files?
faq.answer: No. It supplies planning checks and templates. The host agent or user must run tools and make changes.
